text.text_excerpt: As my companion and I was walking and chatting along Decatur Street toward the French Market, I literally stopped mid-sentence, turned 90 degree and right into the store. Didn't realize I was gone until she asked about lunch and didn't get a response. In my defense, I cannot turn down the allure of fresh made candies. There are plenty stores here that sells pralines, but I like Evans mostly because theirs blood congealing sweet, also they have so many different flavors: original, chocolate, maple, rum, with pecan or coconut or peanut butter. Of course, pralines can't be the only items they carry. There are fudges and assorted sweet treats for any palate. Oh, they are conveniently down the...

So how do you follow up some delicious beignets and coffee from Cafe Du Monde!? With some more delicious pralines and chocolates from Evens Creole Candy, why not I've been walking all day. Evans Creole Candy was one of the many French Quarter establishments I walked through along the mighty Mississippi. I like Evans Creole Candy. They are very nice, organized, clean, and friendly, well everyone in NOLA was very friendly while I was there so awesome job NOLA peeps. So one of the biggest reason I'm a fan is that they gave me free samples, I just had some sweets but hey who's gonna turn down free samples especially if I was gonna buy some. They also make them right in front of you which is a...

There is no shortage of praline/candy shops in New Orleans. But so far, my favorite has been Evans. The shop is clean, organized, and a nice cool escape from the overbearing New Orleans heat. Whether you're buying in bulk or just wanting a quick sweet snack, they've got boxes of up to 50 pralines or a case full of individuals. But, for those who aren't fans of pralines, have no fear, they have a big variety of other delectables available too. From chocolate dipped Oreos to Marshmallow/pecan clusters, you're sure to find something to indulge yourself in!
